facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_正印 (Wood carrying The Sage). Persona The Sage (正印). Definition line: "Nourishment that deepens without redirecting, the root that holds". Keyword Care, charge gentle, poles catalyst Wisdom / friction Comfort. Family function: Mind. Cost dimension: the root that holds; shelter that can become stillness. Arena: roots, old trees, the deep well, inherited warmth. Classical portrait: shelter and nourishment that deepens without redirecting; over-protection, "not ready yet" as a place to stay. Ruled domains: Knowledge, Shelter, Nurture. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 偏印.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Wood generating Fire cross-polarity — reach nourishing warmth and opening direction".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Sage: living shelter, the teaching tree. Care in you grows canopies, patience wide enough for slow learners, roots that hold ground for whole families. What you know, you plant in people. It is the gentlest power in the system. Just keep one sunny patch that grows things purely for you."
- k2_functional: "You think in growth arcs: what this person could become with the right seasons."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Smothering","Clingy","Dormant"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Knowledge":"Your knowledge is arboreal: living, branching, taught best by walking someone through the grove. You learn to pass on. Teaching is how your roots drink.","Shelter":"Your shelter is canopy: people rest under your patience and grow in your shade. The forest never asks who waters the oldest tree. Arrange your own rain.","Nurture":"The nourishing thread runs orchard-deep. Where care came early, you draw on it without thinking. Where it ran thin, you grew your own. Tend your roots with the same hands you use on everyone else’s."}

  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 木_偏印 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Connects dots","Perceptive","Self-taught"],"friction":["Tangled","Secretive","Reclusive"]}
- Sibling cell 木_偏印 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your mind grafts ideas across fields that never formally met. The biology podcast fixes the pricing problem, the poetry course improves your code reviews. Nothing you learn stays in its own bed, and the hybrids that result are yours alone."

Core element Fire, energy element Wood. Law: Wood feeds Fire (木生火: dry branches make the flame). Relative to the core the energy is the feeder, so Wood is this core's Mind. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Wood on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Wood as the Mind is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: What you know is not finished until it is passed on. Since being useful matters more than being ahead, you hand over a lesson the day you learn it. Passing it on costs you the head start, and your knowing comes alive in others.

value_b.text: You pass on what you know before you have finished using it. Because a lesson kept feels like a lesson wasted, you would rather teach it than sit on it. The price is your own advantage, and you have never minded the price.

value.text: Passing it on is your favorite part of knowing. Teaching the thing comes ahead of using it, and the advantage you earned goes to whoever you taught. Keep one thing you know for yourself, because what you pass on first never pays you back.

value.text: You take people in, spare bed and all. Being the safe place is how you feel most yourself, so you would rather shelter someone than be sheltered. You go without a home that is only yours, and the trade feels fair to you.

value_b.text: Taking someone in comes naturally to you. Because a person under your roof feels like a reason to keep going, you say yes ahead of counting the cost. You pay for it in quiet evenings, and the house feels right to you that way.

value.text: Taking people in makes a house matter. You put someone's shelter ahead of your own quiet, and your sleep is the first thing to go. You hand over your rest a night at a time, and being taken in once would hand some back.

value.text: You give a person time rather than a push. A push feels like a way to spoil the growing, so you wait for someone to get there instead of pulling. You see the result last of everyone, and the waiting is the care itself.

value_b.text: You give the slow ones time ahead of advice. Because you trust that a person gets there at their own pace, you keep the push to yourself. You get your results long after your part is done, and that lateness is the price.

value.text: Giving it time is how you respect someone's growth. Waiting for them to get there feels kinder than pulling them, so your own next step stays parked with theirs. You give away the time your chance needed, and it closes while you wait on theirs.

value.text: When someone close to you grows slowly, you give them time instead of a push. Holding back feels more like respect than a nudge, so their nudge never comes. You hold back the push that would have moved them, and it is yours to give.
